question.text: A Composite Insurance Agent may represent insurers subject to which of the following category limits?

answer.text: Not more than 3 life insurers, 3 general insurers and 3 health insurers
Not more than one life insurer, one general insurer, one health insurer, and one each of the mono-line insurers
Not more than 9 insurers in total, with no category restriction
Only one insurer in total across all categories

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-B (p.36), a Composite Insurance Agent may not act for more than one life insurer, one general insurer, one health insurer, and one each of the mono-line insurers. The same page separately describes a composite corporate agent, who is permitted to work with three life, three general, and three health insurers. The Trap: The "3+3+3" limit applies to a composite corporate agent, not a Composite Insurance Agent. A fixed numeric total such as 4 over-specifies the rule because the source uses "one each of the mono-line insurers" — there may be more than one mono-line category. Note: The distinction between Composite Insurance Agent and composite corporate agent is what the question is testing; both terms appear on p.36 with different limits.
